evidence.title: Various antibody clones of Napsin A, TTF-1, and p40 in non-small cell lung carcinoma
evidence.text: This tissue-microarray study evaluated CK5, p63, and p40 as squamous markers and Napsin A and TTF-1 as lung adenocarcinoma markers. Reported performance varied by marker and antibody clone, and combining Napsin A with TTF-1 improved sensitivity.

evidence.title: Immunostaining for TTF-1, Napsin A, p40, and cytokeratin 5 aids differential diagnosis of NSCLC
evidence.text: The study compared marker combinations for separating lung adenocarcinoma from squamous cell carcinoma. TTF-1 and Napsin A supported adenocarcinoma, while p40 and CK5 supported squamous differentiation; the combined panel was more informative than a single stain.

evidence.title: Value of napsin A and thyroid transcription factor-1 in the identification of primary lung adenocarcinoma
evidence.text: In a cohort containing primary lung cancers and metastases, Napsin A and TTF-1 were frequently expressed in primary lung adenocarcinoma. The study also observed TTF-1 expression outside lung adenocarcinoma, supporting interpretation as a panel rather than as an isolated marker.

evidence.title: Educational case: basal cell carcinoma and its histologic differential
evidence.text: Basal cell carcinoma shows dermal islands of basophilic tumor cells with peripheral nuclear palisading, stromal retraction, and loose mucinous stroma. Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma shows invasive islands of pleomorphic keratinocytes arising from the epidermis with prominent nucleoli and increased mitoses. Melanoma can show irregular nests and single pleomorphic pigmented melanocytes within the epidermis and dermis.

evidence.title: Sampling and confirmation in infectious esophagitis
evidence.text: For suspected HSV esophagitis, diagnostic cytopathic changes are most likely at the ulcer edge and in sloughed squamous cells. Candida requires demonstration of pseudohyphae or true hyphae and assessment of tissue invasion rather than isolated budding yeasts in exudate. Histology may require organism-specific immunostaining, in situ hybridization, culture, or special stains for confirmation.

review.assessment: The vision models provide conflicting classifications across multiple organ systems, while the pathology report describes benign breast tissue features with non-specific inflammation, lacking evidence of malignancy.
rationale: The de-identified report describes breast tissue with a ductal structure and inflammatory infiltration, but does not mention irregular nests or desmoplasia required for 'breast invasive carcinoma'.
Vision model outputs are highly discordant, spanning breast, lung, and kidney carcinomas with very low confidence scores (all < 0.20).

Retrieved literature focuses on lung adenocarcinoma/squamous markers [PMID:26447895, PMID:26137020] and skin cancer morphology [PMC:7944528-SkinCancerMorphology], none of which align with the report's description of breast tissue.
discrepancies: Conflict between the report's description of breast tissue and model predictions for lung and kidney carcinomas.
Absence of malignant histological features in the report despite model labels for invasive carcinomas.
recommended_review: Pathologist review of the original slides to determine if the 'inflammatory infiltration' represents a reactive process or a malignancy not captured in the summary report.
limitations: The provided report is descriptive and lacks a definitive diagnosis.
Vision model scores are extremely low, suggesting poor fit for all candidate labels.
